meaning: wildly unreasonable; so illogical as to be ridiculous
note: Asked three times, always as an antonym — the paper wants the sensible/rational side.

meaning: skilful and quick, especially in handling a situation
sentence: The CEO has been praised for his adroit management of the company's financial recovery.
note: 'Ambidextrous' was offered as a trap: it means using both hands equally well, not being skilful.

meaning: struck with sudden shock or horror
sentence: The leader said, "I am aghast with the developments so far. I will take time to understand this."

meaning: loyalty or commitment to a person, group or cause
sentence: The members of the group expressed their allegiance to their leader.

meaning: needing great effort; hard and tiring to do
sentence: It was indeed arduous to cross streets in New York.

meaning: found out for certain; established as fact
sentence: The cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained, but police officials suspect the driver.

meaning: promising success; showing signs that something good will happen
sentence: He was born on a very auspicious day.

meaning: given or presented, especially as an honour
sentence: The highest award was bestowed upon her for her yeoman service.
note: 'Imbibed' was offered as a trap: it means absorbed or drank, not gave.

meaning: shortness, especially of speech or writing
sentence: His speeches were models of brevity.
note: The same paper asked it both ways — once for the synonym, once for the opposite.

meaning: honest and straightforward; saying what one really thinks
sentence: His candid opinions have won him many friends.
note: 'Kind', 'courteous' and 'generous' were traps — they describe manner, not openness.

meaning: worried or troubled; also, involved in and affected by something
sentence: He was quite concerned about his son's career.
note: Two senses, and the papers test both — 'the people concerned' means involved, not worried.

meaning: spreading easily from one person to another, of a disease or a feeling
